gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-bengali: Gobold spreads its geometric letters wide, with curves that never quite close and a single outline-like weight. Noto Serif Bengali settles in beneath with finer hairlines and a dense band of text, so a longer passage moves like brushed ink.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-devanaga: Noto Serif Devanagari has a literary, classic feel, with short ascenders and a big lowercase body. Noto Serif Devanagari handles the reading while Gobold handles the shouting, each stroke of its heading carrying the same visual weight across the line.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-dives-ak: Gobold lays down its commanding letters with a steady pen pressure, curves left open and spaced far apart. Noto Serif Dives Akuru sits next to it softer and more refined, a text serif whose capitals look short beside its tall small letters.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-dogra: Noto Serif Dogra feels bookish and slightly rough, like crayon on paper. Its capitals barely rise above the lowercase, and a faint thick-thin rhythm smooths the pace over a long stretch of reading.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-georgian: Noto Serif Georgian packs its lowercase tight, like coiled rope, with a modest thick-thin difference and an authoritative voice. And Gobold, with no contrast between stems and joins, makes the page feel like a long read in a library.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-gujarati: Noto Serif Gujarati has a bookish, authoritative voice, with oversized e and a counters and strokes that taper only slightly. But Gobold is the one for plain, unshaded lines, spaced wide and commanding, while the serif carries the reading.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-gurmukhi: Editorial and literary, the body here has a generous x-height and a gradual change in weight. Noto Serif Gurmukhi, with medium contrast and no sharp hairlines, makes a softer partner for Gobold's unbroken, commanding stems.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-hebrew: Noto Serif Hebrew reads sturdy and classic, tall in the body and subtly modulated. It sits between monoline strokes and razor-thin hairlines, while Gobold keeps one unit-width stroke throughout, and the body can take a generous size.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-kannada: Traditional and literary, the body font has big counters in a tall lowercase. Noto Serif Kannada, a text serif with soft accents of heavier strokes, could use a slightly larger size beside Gobold's fat crossbars and commanding build.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-khmer: Gobold draws every glyph with an unmodulated line, commanding and geometric. Noto Serif Khmer does the quieter work as a text serif, with tall lowercase close to the capitals and thicks and thins used in moderation.
